name: Romani

ancestors.notes: Descended from Sanskrit/Prakrit; Indo-Aryan language brought to Europe by Roma people from northern India

notes: Romani (Vlax dialect group, standard reference). Indo-Aryan language of the Roma people. Highly diverse with many dialects. Aspirated stops čh, kh, ph, th are distinctive (Sanskrit inheritance). Phonology influenced by contact with European languages. No single standardized orthography; Romani Writing Standard (RWS) used here.

sources.author: Matras, Yaron
sources.title: Romani. In Kortmann & van der Auwera (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of Europe: A Comprehensive Guide, 257-268
sources.publisher: De Gruyter Mouton; author's manuscript on yaronmatras.org
sources.pages: 257-268 (chapter); §2.1 is the third page of the manuscript, which carries no printed numbers
sources.notes: §2.1 Phoneme inventory, read in full. Confirms the inherited five vowels i e a o u, the three-way plosive series p t k / pʰ tʰ kʰ / b d g, the affricates ts tʃ / tʃʰ / dʒ, fricatives f s ʃ χ h and v z, nasals m n, liquids l r, glide j, with ʒ marginal and loanword-bound, and notes a second rhotic (uvular ʀ, velar ɣ or retroflex ɽ) in conservative south-eastern dialects that this map writes ⟨ř⟩ = r. A phonological sketch across dialects, not an orthography: it does not name the Romani Writing Standard letters, so the letter values here stand on the inventory it gives, not on a letter table it does not give. It writes the velar fricative χ where the map writes ⟨x⟩/⟨ch⟩ = x, a symbol difference.

location.notes: Glottolog's representative point for Vlax Romani.
